newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: One-off item upped Argentine Treasury gap - official.
newsitem.headline: One-off item upped Argentine Treasury gap - official.

text.p: A big rise in Argentina's Treasury deficit to $423 million in January came after the central government paid a one-off debt to the provinces, the economy minister's chief advisor said Wednesday.

January's Treasury deficit was 18.4 percent higher than in January 1996, but Carlos Rodriguez said that the jump came after the central government paid the provinces $230 million it owed them from last year's shared tax revenues.
But Rodriguez said the large January Treasury deficit would not knock Argentina's first quarter fiscal targets off track.
"The deficit falls completely within the targets agreed with the International Monetary Fund," he said.

Under the IMF targets, Argentina's fiscal deficit cannot exceed $1.04 billion in the first quarter or $3 billion for the whole of 1997. The year figure does not include a $1.5 billion expenditure due to taking over provincial government pension funds.
No figures on Argentina's fiscal deficit for January have been released yet.
Figures for the Treasury balance do not include the results of certain state agencies, which are included in the overall fiscal balance calculations.
